text:
The power spec is the only failure: 3.504 mW against a 1.4 mW limit. Power is about 1.8 V × (1.937 mA in M2 + 10 µA reference) ≈ 3.50 mW, so the tail current is roughly 2.5× too high. Gain, bandwidth, GBW, swing and output DC all pass with margin, so the fault is in the bias/mirror path, not the signal path.

The sensitivities point to the mirror. M3 has -21.7% power sensitivity and M2 has +19.1%, both close to the ~1/W and ∝W behavior expected from a current mirror with a fixed reference. M1 barely affects power (+0.5%), so it is unlikely to be the fault.

M3 is the most likely corrupted element. Its W/L is 0.793/0.984 ≈ 0.81, so the M2:M3 ratio is about 327, which drives M2 to roughly 1.9 mA. The mirror current scales with L3/W3, so an altered reference length or width pushes the tail current up. M2 is the second candidate because its width sets the mirrored current directly. M1 is least likely.

```json
{"ranking": ["M3", "M2", "M1"], "fault": "Mirror reference M3 mis-sized (W=0.793 um, L=0.984 um, W/L about 0.81 vs a matched mirror ratio), inflating the M2:M3 mirror ratio to about 327 and pushing the tail current in M2 to about 1.94 mA (total about 3.5 mW). M3 should be resized so the mirror delivers roughly 0.7 mA or less (for example, matched L and a smaller W/L) to meet the 1.4 mW limit."}
```
